passages.text: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our forefathers were all under the cloud, and that they all passed through the sea.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Christian brothers.
He does not want them to be unaware.
He reminds them about their forefathers.
All their forefathers were under the cloud.
All their forefathers passed through the sea.
passages.original: Οὐ θέλω γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν ἀδελφοί ὅτι οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν πάντες ὑπὸ τὴν νεφέλην ἦσαν καὶ πάντες διὰ τῆς θαλάσσης διῆλθον

passages.text: They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Corinthian church.
He reminds them about the Israelites.
All the Israelites followed Moses.
God led them with a cloud.
God brought them through the sea.
All the Israelites shared in these events.
All the Israelites were baptized into Moses.
This happened in the cloud and in the sea.
passages.original: καὶ πάντες εἰς τὸν Μωϋσῆν ἐβαπτίσαντο ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ καὶ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ

passages.text: They all ate the same spiritual food and drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.
passages.sermon:
All our forefathers ate the same spiritual food.
All our forefathers drank the same spiritual drink.
They drank from a spiritual rock that went with them.
That rock was Christ.
passages.original: καὶ πάντες τὸ αὐτὸ πνευματικὸν βρῶμα ἔφαγον καὶ πάντες τὸ αὐτὸ πνευματικὸν ἔπιον πόμα ἔπινον γὰρ ἐκ πνευματικῆς ἀκολουθούσης πέτρας ἡ πέτρα δὲ ἦν ὁ Χριστός

passages.text: Nevertheless, God was not pleased with most of them, for they were struck down in the wilderness.
passages.sermon: God was not pleased with most of the Israelites.\r\nGod struck them down in the wilderness.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐν τοῖς πλείοσιν αὐτῶν εὐδόκησεν ὁ Θεός κατεστρώθησαν γὰρ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ

passages.text: These things took place as examples to keep us from craving evil things as they did.
passages.sermon:
God gave examples to us through these events.
God wants us to learn from these examples.
God does not want us to desire evil things.
The people before us desired evil things.
We must not desire evil things as they did.
passages.original: Ταῦτα δὲ τύποι ἡμῶν ἐγενήθησαν εἰς τὸ μὴ εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἐπιθυμητὰς κακῶν καθὼς κἀκεῖνοι ἐπεθύμησαν

passages.text: Do not be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written: “The people sat down to eat and to drink, and got up to indulge in revelry.”
passages.sermon:
God warned the people of Israel in the wilderness.
Some of them became idolaters.
Do not become idolaters.
Scripture says, “The people sat down to eat and to drink.”
Then they got up to indulge in revelry.
passages.original: μηδὲ εἰδωλολάτραι γίνεσθε καθώς τινες αὐτῶν ὥσπερ γέγραπται Ἐκάθισεν ὁ λαὸς φαγεῖν καὶ πεῖν καὶ ἀνέστησαν παίζειν

passages.text: We should not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and in one day twenty-three thousand of them died.
passages.sermon:
Paul warns the church in Corinth.
He speaks to Christians.
He says, “We should not commit sexual immorality.”
Some people in Israel committed sexual immorality.
God judged them.
In one day, twenty-three thousand of them died.
passages.original: μηδὲ πορνεύωμεν καθώς τινες αὐτῶν ἐπόρνευσαν καὶ ἔπεσαν μιᾷ ἡμέρᾳ εἰκοσι τρεῖς χιλιάδες

passages.text: We should not test Christ, as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.
passages.sermon: We should not test Christ.\r\nSome people in the past tested Christ.\r\nSnakes killed those people.
passages.original: μηδὲ ἐκπειράζωμεν τὸν Χριστόν καθώς τινες αὐτῶν ἐπείρασαν καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ὄφεων ἀπώλλυντο

passages.text: And do not complain, as some of them did, and were killed by the destroying angel.
passages.sermon:
Do not complain.
Some people in the past complained.
God sent the destroying angel.
The destroying angel killed those people.
passages.original: μηδὲ γογγύζετε καθάπερ τινὲς αὐτῶν ἐγόγγυσαν καὶ ἀπώλοντο ὑπὸ τοῦ ὀλοθρευτοῦ

passages.text: Now these things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come.
passages.sermon:
God gave examples to the people of Israel in the past.
These things happened to them as lessons.
God caused these events to be written down.
God wrote them for our instruction.
We are the people living at the time when the fulfillment of the ages has come.
God warns us through these examples and writings.
passages.original: Ταῦτα δὲ τυπικῶς συνέβαινεν ἐκείνοις ἐγράφη δὲ πρὸς νουθεσίαν ἡμῶν εἰς οὓς τὰ τέλη τῶν αἰώνων κατήντηκεν

passages.text: So the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Corinth.
He warns people who feel confident in their faith.
Anyone who thinks he stands firm must watch himself.
He must be careful not to fall.
passages.original: Ὥστε ὁ δοκῶν ἑστάναι βλεπέτω μὴ πέσῃ

passages.text: No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.
passages.sermon:
God is faithful.
You face temptation.
Your temptation is not unique.
Your temptation is common to all people.
God will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear.
When you are tempted, God will provide a way out.
You will be able to endure temptation.
passages.original: πειρασμὸς ὑμᾶς οὐκ εἴληφεν εἰ μὴ ἀνθρώπινος πιστὸς δὲ ὁ Θεός ὃς οὐκ ἐάσει ὑμᾶς πειρασθῆναι ὑπὲρ ὃ δύνασθε ἀλλὰ ποιήσει σὺν τῷ πειρασμῷ καὶ τὴν ἔκβασιν τοῦ δύνασθαι ὑπενεγκεῖν

passages.text: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Christians in Corinth.
He calls them his beloved.
He gives them a command.
He says, “Flee from idolatry.”
He tells them to avoid worshiping idols.
He urges them to stay away from false gods.
passages.original: Διόπερ ἀγαπητοί μου φεύγετε ἀπὸ τῆς εἰδωλολατρίας

passages.text: I speak to reasonable people; judge for yourselves what I say.
passages.sermon:
I speak to you.
You are reasonable people.
You can understand.
Judge for yourselves what I say.
passages.original: ὡς φρονίμοις λέγω κρίνατε ὑμεῖς ὅ φημι

passages.text: Is not the cup of blessing that we bless a participation in the blood of Christ? And is not the bread that we break a participation in the body of Christ?
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Christians in Corinth.
Paul calls them to avoid idolatry.
Paul reminds them about the Lord’s Supper.
We bless the cup of blessing.
This cup is a sharing in the blood of Christ.
We break the bread.
This bread is a sharing in the body of Christ.
passages.original: Τὸ ποτήριον τῆς εὐλογίας ὃ εὐλογοῦμεν οὐχὶ κοινωνία ἐστὶν τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ τὸν ἄρτον ὃν κλῶμεν οὐχὶ κοινωνία τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐστιν

passages.text: Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Christians.
Christians share one loaf of bread.
This loaf is a symbol.
The loaf shows unity.
Many people belong to Christ.
All Christians form one body.
All Christians eat from the same loaf.
This shared loaf makes them one body.
passages.original: ὅτι εἷς ἄρτος ἓν σῶμα οἱ πολλοί ἐσμεν οἱ γὰρ πάντες ἐκ τοῦ ἑνὸς ἄρτου μετέχομεν

passages.text: Consider the people of Israel: Are not those who eat the sacrifices fellow partakers in the altar?
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel are a nation chosen by God.
They offer animal sacrifices to God according to the law.
Some Israelites eat the meat from these sacrifices.
These people share in the altar when they eat the sacrifices.
Eating the sacrifices makes them participants in the altar.
passages.original: βλέπετε τὸν Ἰσραὴλ κατὰ σάρκα οὐχ οἱ ἐσθίοντες τὰς θυσίας κοινωνοὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου εἰσίν

passages.text: Am I suggesting, then, that food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
He addresses food sacrificed to idols.
He asks a question.
He says, “Am I saying that food offered to idols is something important?”
He also asks, “Am I saying that an idol is something real?”
passages.original: Τί οὖν φημι ὅτι εἰδωλόθυτόν τί ἐστιν ἢ ὅτι εἴδωλόν τί ἐστιν

passages.text: No, but the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God. And I do not want you to be participants with demons.
passages.sermon:
Pagans offer sacrifices to demons.
Pagans do not offer sacrifices to God.
I do not want you to share with demons.
I do not want you to become participants with demons.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ ὅτι ἃ θύουσιν τὰ ἔθνη δαιμονίοις καὶ οὐ Θεῷ θύουσιν οὐ θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς κοινωνοὺς τῶν δαιμονίων γίνεσθαι

passages.text: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too; you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Christians.
Paul says you cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons.
You cannot share in the table of the Lord and the table of demons.
You must choose one.
You cannot belong to both.
passages.original: οὐ δύνασθε ποτήριον Κυρίου πίνειν καὶ ποτήριον δαιμονίων οὐ δύνασθε τραπέζης Κυρίου μετέχειν καὶ τραπέζης δαιμονίων

passages.text: Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Christians in Corinth.
Paul warns about provoking the Lord.
He asks, “Are we trying to make the Lord jealous?”
He asks, “Are we stronger than the Lord?”
We are not stronger than the Lord.
passages.original: ἢ παραζηλοῦμεν τὸν Κύριον μὴ ἰσχυρότεροι αὐτοῦ ἐσμεν

passages.text: “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is edifying.
passages.sermon:
God gives us freedom to do many things.
Everything is permissible.
Not everything is beneficial.
Everything is permissible.
Not everything builds up or strengthens others.
passages.original: Πάντα ἔξεστιν ἀλλ’ οὐ πάντα συμφέρει Πάντα ἔξεστιν ἀλλ’ οὐ πάντα οἰκοδομεῖ

passages.text: No one should seek his own good, but the good of others.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians in Corinth.
\r\nHe teaches about how to live among others.
\r\nNo one should seek only his own good.
\r\nEach person should seek the good of others.
passages.original: μηδεὶς τὸ ἑαυτοῦ ζητείτω ἀλλὰ τὸ τοῦ ἑτέρου

passages.text: Eat anything sold in the meat market without raising questions of conscience, for, “The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof.”
passages.sermon:
God owns the earth.
God owns everything in it.
You may eat anything sold in the meat market.
Do not ask questions about it because of your conscience.
passages.original: Πᾶν τὸ ἐν μακέλλῳ πωλούμενον ἐσθίετε μηδὲν ἀνακρίνοντες διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν Τοῦ Κυρίου γὰρ Ἡ γῆ καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς

passages.text: If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat anything set before you without raising questions of conscience.
passages.sermon:
An unbeliever may invite you to a meal.
You may want to go to this meal.
Eat anything that is set before you at this meal.
Do not ask questions about the food because of conscience.
passages.original: Εἴ τις καλεῖ ὑμᾶς τῶν ἀπίστων καὶ θέλετε πορεύεσθαι πᾶν τὸ παρατιθέμενον ὑμῖν ἐσθίετε μηδὲν ἀνακρίνοντες διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν

passages.text: But if someone tells you, “This food was offered to idols,” then do not eat it, for the sake of the one who told you and for the sake of conscience— the other one’s conscience, I mean, not your own. For why should my freedom be determined by someone else’s conscience?
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians in Corinth.
He teaches about eating food offered to idols.
If someone says to you, “This food was offered to idols,” do not eat it.
Do not eat it for the sake of the person who told you.
Do not eat it for the sake of conscience.
I mean the other person’s conscience, not your own.
My freedom should not be judged by another person’s conscience.
passages.original: ἐὰν δέ τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ Τοῦτο ἱερόθυτόν ἐστιν μὴ ἐσθίετε δι’ ἐκεῖνον τὸν μηνύσαντα καὶ τὴν συνείδησιν συνείδησιν δὲ λέγω οὐχὶ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἀλλὰ τὴν τοῦ ἑτέρου ἵνα‿ τί γὰρ ἡ ἐλευθερία μου κρίνεται ὑπὸ ἄλλης συνειδήσεως

passages.text: If I partake in the meal with thankfulness, why am I denounced because of that for which I give thanks?
passages.sermon:
I eat this meal with thankfulness.
I give thanks for this food.
Why do people speak against me for eating what I thank God for?
I do not deserve blame for being thankful.
My gratitude should not cause others to judge me.
passages.original: εἰ ἐγὼ χάριτι μετέχω τί βλασφημοῦμαι ὑπὲρ οὗ ἐγὼ εὐχαριστῶ

passages.text: So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians in Corinth.
Paul teaches about daily actions.
You may eat.
You may drink.
You may do anything else.
Do everything for the glory of God.
passages.original: Εἴτε οὖν ἐσθίετε εἴτε πίνετε εἴτε τι ποιεῖτε πάντα εἰς δόξαν Θεοῦ ποιεῖτε

passages.text: Do not become a stumbling block, whether to Jews or Greeks or the church of God— as I also try to please everyone in all I do. For I am not seeking my own good, but the good of many, that they may be saved.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul urges believers to avoid causing others to stumble.
Do not become a stumbling block to Jews.
Do not become a stumbling block to Greeks.
Do not become a stumbling block to the church of God.
Paul tries to please everyone in all he does.
Paul does not seek his own benefit.
Paul seeks the good of many people.
Paul wants many people to be saved.
passages.original: ἀπρόσκοποι καὶ Ἰουδαίοις γίνεσθε καὶ Ἕλλησιν καὶ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ καθὼς κἀγὼ πάντα πᾶσιν ἀρέσκω μὴ ζητῶν τὸ ἐμαυτοῦ σύμφορον ἀλλὰ τὸ τῶν πολλῶν ἵνα σωθῶσιν
